article_text:
On-location production is still declining in the Los Angeles area, even if California’s Film & Television Tax Credit Program is propping up much of what’s left.

Per the latest report from FilmLA , on-location filming accounted for 4,171 shoot days from July through September 2026, which is a 4.8% decrease from the same period last year. However, the organization also finds that the state’s tax incentive is accounting for about 40.3% of scripted, on-location production during that time — nearly doubling the share from a year ago.

Made In L.A., The Paramount Strategy: ‘Clueless’ Series & Viola Davis’ ‘Ascent’ Among Recipients In Latest California TV Tax Credit Allocations

Television is benefitting the most from incentivized productions. Projects that were accepted into the program made up 62% of all TV comedy shoot days and 49.4% of TV drama shoot days (up from 19% and 20.6%, respectively) during the same time last year.

This doesn’t quite tell the full story, since television production, particularly on comedies, often largely takes place on soundstages, which are not captured in this data. Soundstage occupancy also remains far below the levels it once maintained a decade ago.

Watch on Deadline

Incentivized TV series that shot in L.A. last quarter included A Hundred Percent (Netflix), Baywatch (Fox), Mr & Mrs. Smith (Amazon), Shrinking (Warner Bros. TV/Apple TV+), High Potential (ABC), The Night Agent (Sony Pictures Television/Netflix), Tracker (CBS), I Love LA (HBO), and Rooster (HBO).

Feature films finished the third quarter with 533 shoot days, a marginal 2.1% increase from the same period last year. Incentivized projects account for 24.4% of that total, the majority of which are independent. However, there are a few studio films in the mix including 13 Going on 30 (Netflix), Cut Off (Warner Bros.) and They Follow (Neon).

Commercials marked the largest decline, down 15.9% to on-location 562 shoot days during the third quarter, although those are not covered by California’s tax credit program.

On-location production in Los Angeles has been on a decline for years , and the trend has continued despite California’s massive efforts to expand the state’s tax incentive program last year. Not only did lawmakers raise the cap to $750 million annually, the revamped bill also significantly expanded program eligibility. Granted, this quarter’s decline is smaller than Q2’s 13% slip .

article_text:
Each week we highlight the noteworthy titles that have recently hit streaming platforms in the United States. Check out this week’s selections below and past round-ups here .

Ali G: Who Iz I? (Sacha Baron Cohen)

After a perfunctory, slimmed-down theatrical release last weekend, Sacha Baron Cohen’s feature directorial debut has now arrived on Prime Video. Anyone familiar with the comedian’s hijinks, and particularly Borat 2 and Who Is America? , will know what to expect when it comes to this Ali G sequel: a clunky and strained (albeit sporadically funny) reckoning with modern political and societal ills that feels a little too late to the game to pack a genuinely hilarious punch. As streaming slop, one could get much worse, but especially with his last few projects, it feels like Baron Cohen is seemingly content with shooting fish in a barrel.

Where to Stream: Prime Video

American Doctor (Poh Si Teng)

Poh Si Teng’s American Doctor is a harrowing, heartbreaking portrait of Palestinian, Jewish, and Zoroastrian doctors who are risking their lives to tend to the overwhelming victims of the ongoing genocide in Gaza and speak the truth in any way they can. Dan Mecca said in his Sundance review , “When will this end? When will this bloodshed stop? And when will the United States of America stop supporting it? Filmmaker Poh Si Teng offers a clear-eyed, unrelenting look at the genocide in Gaza with her documentary American Doctor . It follows three doctors––Dr. Feroze Sidhwa, Dr. Thaer Ahmad, and Dr. Mark Perlmutter––that are consistently trying to save lives in the Gaza Strip. On some trips they are approved to enter. On others they are denied for specious reasons. Dr. Perlmutter is Jewish, Dr. Sidhwa is Zoroastrian, and Dr. Ahmad is Palestinian. Their mission is the mission of all medical professionals: to heal everyone they can.”

Where to Stream: Watermelon+ (for free through November 6 only)

Black Zombie (Maya Annik Bedward)

More than reclaiming the zombie motif from the knee-jerk response that Night of the Living Dead inhibited, Maya Annik Bedward’s Black Zombie is a reclamation of Vodou from the colonial fear-mongering that used it to demonize Black people the world over. Because it’s 2026 and Haitians are still cautious to admit their connection to the religion. There’s still an outsider belief that Haiti’s recent hardships are a result of its ancestors making a pact with the Devil. – Jared M. ( full review )

Where to Stream: Kino Film Collection

The Dog Stars (Ridley Scott)

The Dog Stars —an adaptation of Peter Heller’s hit novel of the same name—follows Hig, aka “Big Hig” (Jacob Elordi), a thirty-something everyman mechanic who lost his pregnant wife to the flu virus that wiped out most of the world. He lives alongside his dog, Jasper, in an airport hangar outside of Denver. His only companion is Bangley (Josh Brolin), another survivor who, unlike Hig, is content with the quaint, gray, quiet life they lead (which doesn’t look terribly different from some rural American living situations today). To Bangley, protecting property is paramount and the very concept of new faces invites trouble. Hig, however, is willing to brave that dark; the risk of unknown danger weighs less to him than the potential benefit of discovering a community. And he has a lead. – Luke H. ( full review )

Where to Stream: VOD

Filipiñana (Rafael Manuel)

When Janine (Nour Hooshmand) asks Isabel (Jorrybell Agoto) what the Ilocos region of the Philippines is like—she’s only ever heard it was beautiful without having visited herself—she explains that many spots look and feel just like the posh golf course where they work. What should just be a point of comparison to better understand an unknown, however, is soon revealed as a very purposeful juxtaposition. – Jared M. ( full review )

Where to Stream: VOD

If I Go Will They Miss Me (Walter Thompson-Hernández)

Finding poetic beauty in the quotidian, Walter Thompson-Hernández’s If I Go Will They Miss Me centers on coming of age in housing projects of southern Los Angeles. It’s a way of life often depicted with a grittiness that favors do-or-die intensity, yet this emerging director of great promise takes an opposite approach. One where dreams of flight are always on the mind as the planes coming in and out of nearby LAX are constantly passing above. Greek gods, as studied in school, give purpose to a higher calling. An affection and adoration for and from its ensemble (many non-professionals, in this case) form a portrait of a living, loving community that rises above hardship. Just as his characters draw grand personal inspiration, Thompson-Hernández is greatly indebted to a variety of renowned directors, including Barry Jenkins, RaMell Ross, Charles Burnett, and Spike Lee, with the end result a film greater than the sum of its recognizable influences. Continue reading my full review .

Where to Stream: VOD

Mum, I’m Alien Pregnant (THUNDERLIPS)

A highlight as part of the Sundance midnight section earlier this year, the New Zealand oddity Mum, I’m Alien Pregnant takes its premise—a slacker getting, as promised, extraterrestrially pregnant—to its ultimate conclusion. It’s a B-movie delight that also voices quite a bit about what often goes unsaid around social and personal fears surrounding physical and emotional changes during pregnancy.

Where to Stream: VOD

Never After Dark (Dave Boyle)

Clearly inspired by Kiyoshi Kurosawa (including casting his frequent collaborator Mutsuo Yoshioka and going so far to plan a remake of Pulse ), Dave Boyle’s creepy chiller Never After Dark is a stylish yet thoughtful pre-October treat. Following a traveling psychic who uncovers dark secrets at a remote house, Boyle’s Japanese production may take its time to deliver the goods, but when the blood spills, it is done in quite memorable fashion.

Where to Stream: VOD

Seeds (Brittany Shyne)

Evoking Gordon Park’s black-and-white photographs of the New Deal Era, cinematographer Brittany Shyne’s powerful debut feature Seeds offers a portrait of a disappearing way of life for Black farmers in the American South. Its casual approach mostly reflects rhythms of life in a vérité style that’s occasionally broken when the camera is acknowledged. – John F. ( full review )

Where to Stream: PBS

article_text:
A Series of Artistic Exhibitions across East Africa

The Goethe-Institut supports Sudanese artists in the region by fostering local artistic networks, professional exchange, and sustainable structures of inclusion.

The Goethe-Instituts in Kenya, Rwanda, & Ethiopia, and the Goethe Centres in Uganda and South Sudan are organizing a series of exhibitions named Networks of Belonging to support Sudanese artists exiled in the East Africa region.

Following an open call, five artists based in each of the five countries were selected: Hussein Merghani Hussein (Addis Abeba), Juma Moris (Juba), Hamza Tirab (Kampala), Mohamed Ibrahim (Kigali), and Sannad Sharif (Nairobi).

The ongoing civil war in Sudan has displaced many artists. In collaboration with Goethe-Institut Khartoum, the Networks of Belonging project responds to this by fostering local artistic networks, professional exchange, and sustainable structures of inclusion. As part of the joint venture, each of the selected artists is granted a production budget to develop new artworks and include them in the exhibition.

The Institute in Khartoum, Sudan, remains closed since 2023 until further notice. The Goethe-Institut Sudan’s cultural program activities, however, continue and are being coordinated from Cairo. This creates virtual and in-person spaces for Sudanese partners, artists, and cultural professionals where intergenerational and interactive dialogue and exchange among Sudanese communities can take place and creativity can be fostered.

The Network of Belonging exhibitions are scheduled to take place between July and November 2026. The exhibition in Nairobi by Sannad Sharif: Indigo Hypoxia will open on 2 nd July 2026.

About Indigo Hypoxia

Indigo Hypoxia is conceived as an immersive solo exhibition—a space that brings together painting, textile installation, and live performance. It presents a series of presences: alienated blue figures existing within a purple atmosphere. The exhibition explores an internal psychological state shaped by a sense of spatial and emotional void. This is not a literal room, but a mental enclosure in which the figures are suspended—caught between withdrawal and exposure, fragility and weight. They do not simply occupy the space; they embody it.

The central question of the exhibition emerges through this tension: what does it mean to feel internally blue while existing within a purple exterior? “My work is an instinctive conversation between myself, the materials, and the moment. I do not plan what I will paint or sculpt—the brush moves first, the colors arrive on their own, and I follow. This process allows me to discover what the work wants to be, rather than forcing it into a predetermined form,” says Sannad Sharif.

In den dort gezeigten Kurz-, Dokumentar- und Spielfilmen geht es nicht nur um Fragen der kurdischen Identität oder Zugehörigkeit, sondern auch um Familie, Freunde, Liebe und Humor. Das Festival findet im Filmhaus Köln und im Filmforum NRW statt.

Sichtbarkeit ist auch im Kino eine wichtige Größe. Dazu tragen Filmfestivals bei, etwa das Kurdische Filmfestival in Köln, das den oft übersehenen kurdischen Perspektiven Raum gibt. Das Festival findet vom 12. bis 16. November im Filmhaus statt. „Mit den Kurdischen Filmtagen möchten wir die Vielfalt des kurdischen Filmschaffens zeigen und Filmschaffenden eine Plattform bieten“, heißt es auf der Webseite. Dabei gehe es nicht nur um Identität, Herkunft und Zugehörigkeit, sondern auch um Familie, Freundschaft, Liebe und Humor. Kurdisches Kino soll in seiner „ganzen Vielfalt“ präsentiert und nicht nur auf „Konflikte und politische Themen“ reduziert werden.

Kurzfilme, Dokus, Fiction

Eröffnet wird das Festival am 12. November im Filmforum NRW mit dem Dokumentarfilm „ The Phantom Pain of Rojava “, der vier verwundete kurdische Guerillakämpfer begleitet. Einst wurden sie als Helden im Kampf gegen den IS gefeiert, doch heute fühlen sie sich von ihren Verbündeten im Stich gelassen. Die Regisseurin Maryam Ebrahimi steht nach der Filmvorführung für Fragen bereit.

Während tagsüber Kurzfilme laufen, rücken abends Langfilme ins Zentrum. Der Dokumentarfilm „ You Don’t Look Nothing Alike “ von Eva Świątkowski erzählt von einem Zufluchtsort für die kurdische Bevölkerung; in „ Rootless Resident “ geht es um einen armenisch-türkisch-kurdischen Schmied. „ The Taste of Sugar “ erzählt fünf Jahre nach dem Ende des Krieges gegen den IS von einem ehemaligen kurdischen Krieger, der noch immer über seinen gefallenen jüngeren Bruder trauert.

Der Spielfilm „ Rauf “ erzählt von einem Jungen, der eine erste große, platonische Liebe erlebt. Und in „ Earth Song “ von Erol Mintaş steht eine Ärztin im Zentrum, die in den Krisengebieten unermüdlich tätig ist, sich darüber aber von ihrer Familie entfremdet hat. Als ihr Vater sie unerwartet aufsucht, muss sie sich ihrer schmerzhaften Vergangenheit stellen. „Earth Song“ ist der Abschlussfilm des Festivals; der Regisseur Erol Mintaş steht anschließend für Fragen bereit.

In einer Masterclass gibt die kurdische Regisseurin Milena Aboyan Einblicke in ihre Arbeit und wie sie sich als migrantische Filmemacherin in Deutschland behauptet. Am 16. November endet das Festival mit einer Lesung von Karosh Taha aus ihrem Roman „ Gulistan “.

Alle Filme werden in der Originalsprache mit englischen Untertiteln gezeigt. Ermöglicht wird das Kurdische Filmfestival durch die Unterstützung von Soziokultur NRW, dem Kulturamt der Stadt Köln, dem Filmforum NRW sowie dem Filmhaus Köln.

Hinweis

Weitere Informationen und das vollständige Programm sowie der Festival-Flyer finden sich auf der Webseite des Filmhauses Köln.

article_text:
Ali Abbas Zafar’s romantic action-drama pairing “Saiyaara” breakout Ahaan Panday with Sharvari will be called “ Beparwah ,” Yash Raj Films revealed Monday.

The title reveal came exactly five months before the film opens worldwide in theaters on March 26, 2027, the Good Friday holiday. Aditya Chopra produces. “Beparwah” is the first time Panday and Sharvari have shared the screen.

'High Potential' Lands Post-Super Bowl LXI Slot on ABC Next February

Until Monday, the film had been known only as Zafar’s untitled next. Yash Raj Films first set the March 2027 date in July, while the production was shooting in the U.K., where much of the film was made.

“Beparwah” reunites Zafar with Chopra for a fifth time. Their earlier collaborations were romantic comedy “Mere Brother Ki Dulhan” (2011), crime drama “Gunday” (2014), wrestling drama “Sultan” (2016) and spy thriller “Tiger Zinda Hai” (2017). The last two, both toplined by Salman Khan, were blockbusters for the banner. Zafar co-wrote the script with Chopra.

Popular on Variety

Since “Tiger Zinda Hai,” Zafar has directed Khan again in “Bharat” (2019), created the Prime Video political series “Tandav” (2021) and helmed “Bade Miyan Chote Miyan” (2024), an Akshay Kumar and Tiger Shroff action vehicle.

Panday made his screen debut in Mohit Suri’s “Saiyaara,” a YRF musical romance opposite fellow newcomer Aneet Padda that became one of the biggest Bollywood hits of 2025. It grossed more than $65 million worldwide and became the highest-grossing Indian love story on record. Panday is the nephew of actor Chunky Panday and a cousin of actor Ananya Panday.

Sharvari launched her career in YRF’s “Bunty Aur Babli 2” (2021) and broke through with the 2024 horror-comedy “Munjya,” which crossed $14 million at the box office. This July, she starred opposite Alia Bhatt in “Alpha,” the first female-led entry in YRF’s spy universe franchise.

The “Beparwah” cast also includes Bobby Deol, Sharvari’s “Alpha” co-star, and Aaishvary Thackeray, grandson of Shiv Sena party founder Bal Thackeray, who plays the antagonist.

Founded in 1970 by the late Yash Chopra and now run by his son Aditya, YRF is one of India’s leading studios. Its spy universe, which includes Zafar’s “Tiger Zinda Hai,” also spans the “War” and “Pathaan” films.

article_text:
Doug Belgrad is departing Netflix where he has been Vice President of Film for more than two years. His exit, which was confirmed by the streamer, is part of the major layoffs at Netflix today that are impacting 1,000 people.

Ironically, Belgrad was Head of Film Dan Lin‘s first hire after a round of layoffs when Lin replaced Scott Stuber and restructured Netflix’s film department.

Related Stories

List Of Hollywood & Media Layoffs From Paramount To Warner Bros Discovery To CNN & More

Netflix Layoffs Underway, Streamer Cutting 1,000 Jobs, 6% Of Workforce

While at Netflix, Belgrad supervised a team of 35 production executives including Film VPs Kira Goldberg and Jason Young as well as VP of Original Studio Film Ori Murmur. Belgrad also worked on more than 50 movies during his short run at the streamer.

Belgrad’s departure is said to be part of a greater restructure by the streamer to reposition resources for the future. The streamer has faced increased competition of late and slower growth. Wall Street has increasingly examined Netflix’s viewer engagement, which upticked only 2% over the first half of the year to 97 billion hours viewed.

Watch on Deadline

RELATED: Netflix Film Executive Sheroum Kim Leaving As Part Of Layoffs

That said, there had been rumblings about the motion picture division of late, including chatter that former Warner Bros. Studio heads Michael De Luca and Pam Abdy may be going over to the streamer. However, sources stress that their recent lunches with Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos were merely on a peer basis. Netflix would need to make a fire breathing commitment to theatrical for De Luca and Abdy to make the segue to the streamer after getting passed over by Skydance co-CEO David Ellison for top posts at the combined Paramount-Warner Bros feature operation.

In an effort to raise the profiles of their movies more, Netflix for the first time is committing to longer windows (on specific titles) in theaters and will be reporting grosses on upcoming pics like Cannes winner La Bola Negra , David Fincher’s The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, Peter Berg’s Mosquito Bowl, Danny Boyle’s Ink, Greta Gerwig’s Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew and animated title Charlie vs. the Chocolate Factory . Previously, Netflix largely used theatrical as a means to qualify movies for awards consideration. Their increased embrace of theatrical comes in the wake of losing their bid to buy Warner Bros. Studios.

RELATED: Lisa Lang McMullen, James Oh, Andrew McQuinn & Carolina Garcia Among Netflix TV Execs Impacted By Layoffs

When Belgrad arrived at Netflix, there was the challenge to make movies at a lower cost. Lin and Belgrad built a slate of titles through 2028. Belgrad focused much of his time on shepherding filmmakers through post-production.

Former top Sony executive Belgrad also tended to Sony’s output deal at Netflix. In addition to the $7B Pay-1 agreement with Netflix for indie studio’s theatrical films, the pact also called for Sony to funnel a number of direct-to-streaming movies to Netflix (the Culver City lot was responsible for the streamer’s most watched movie ever Kpop Demon Hunters, which also doubled as Netflix’s first movie to open at No. 1 at the weekend box office in late August 2025). Belgrad worked with Sony leadership of Tom Rothman, Sanford Panitch and Elizabeth Gabler, to identify which pictures would fill direct-to-Netflix slots. These movies included People We Meet on Vacation, Voicemails from Isabelle (51M views in 11 days), and 72 Hours starring Kevin Hart. Other direct Sony-to-Netflix movies in the pipeline are Grown Ups 3 (Belgrad was the exec on the first two movies at Sony), Matter of Time with Ben Stiller, and Yeti starring Chris Pine.

During his Netflix run, Belgrad was instrumental in packaging such movies as Extraction 3 , Protecting Jared (starring Jason Momoa and Andy Samberg), War Machine (147M views), The Rip (136M views), Happy Gilmore 2 , The Serpent and the Snake, Unabomber (starring Russell Crowe), 13 Going on 30 , Jennifer Lopez and Brett Goldstein’s Office Romance (58M views), Remarkably Bright Christmas, 2034 (AI cautionary tale directed and written by Joseph Gordon Levitt and starring Rachel McAdams), Whisper Man and an untitled David O. Russell movie (both starring Robert De Niro), Ugly Kitten and Double Bind (starring Will Smith).

Belgrad also worked with top filmmakers at Netflix including but to limited to Greta Gerwig, Guillermo del Toro, Peter Berg, Rian Johnson, Christopher McQuarrie, Eva Longoria, Antoine Fuqua, Cameron Crowe and Amy Sherman Palladino.

Before joining Netflix in May 2024, Belgrad spent 25 years at Sony Pictures, and was ultimately co-president under Amy Pascal. He joined the Culver City lot in 1989 and was promoted to co-president of production at Columbia in 2003 and president in 2008. He shepherded the Men in Black franchise, the Adam Sandler canon at Sony, and Oscar-nominated American Hustle and Captain Phillips , to name a few.

Upon stepping down from Sony as President of the Motion Picture Group in 2016, he formed 2.0 Entertainment, which was key in producing and co-financing such Sony movies as Gran Turismo and the last two Bad Boys, 2024’s Bad Boys: Ride Or Die and Bad Boys for Life, the latter a massive pre-Covid hit grossing $426.5M and the highest in the Smith and Martin Lawrence franchise.

Belgrad is still the Chairman of 2.0. He’s not planning to promptly reunite with his former colleagues there, but a producing future isn’t out of the question. 2.0 is an active producer with not just Sony, but Paramount as well, co-financing such titles as the latter’s The Heart of the Beast, Primate, and the upcoming Children of Blood and Bone.

article_text:
Faceless workers and a tsunami of Post-it notes: the surreal world of Japan’s salarymen – in pictures

In his photographic series Ganbatte, Copenhagen-based Argentinian visual artist Jairo Alvarez explores the juxtaposition and harmony between Japan’s relentless work culture and its traditions, connection to nature and faith.

The exhibition features as part of the Head On photo festival 2026 on the Bondi beach promenade from 6 to 29 November

Ganbatte

All photographs by Jairo Alvarez

Mon 9 Nov 2026 09.00 EST

Jōhatsu

Jōhatsu is a Japanese term meaning ‘evaporation.’ It refers to people who suddenly disappear from their lives, leaving jobs, families and identities behind, often due to social pressures, debt or a desire to start over anonymously

Asphyxia

Omamori

Omamori is a Japanese term referring to amulets or talismans that are often sold at Shinto shrines and Buddhist temples in Japan. These amulets are believed to provide various forms of protection or good luck to the bearer. The word

omamori itself can be translated as ‘protection’ or ‘charm’. They are typically displayed and sold at small stands or counters, often near the main hall or entrance of a shrine or temple, where visitors can see and choose from different types of

omamori depending on the blessing they seek

Yūyake

Ritual

chanoyu ,

chadō or

sadō (the way of tea) is a traditional ritual centred on the preparation and sharing of matcha (powdered green tea). Rooted in Zen Buddhist philosophy, it emphasises harmony, respect, purity and tranquillity through the host’s deliberate movements and the guests’ mindful attention. Every element, from the utensils to the seasonal decorations, is chosen to create a moment of quiet simplicity

Nomunication

nomu (meaning ‘to drink’) with ‘communication’ and reflects the tradition of forging connections over drinks. Over time, this practice has shaped workplace dynamics and, consequently, recruitment strategies

Great wave

Extra hours

Ganbatte

ganbatte reflects the importance of perseverance and collective support. It serves as a reminder to individuals that their efforts are recognised and that they have the strength to overcome difficulties and achieve their goals

As the World Series got underway, MCU fans were treated to a new sneak peek at Avengers: Doomsday , premiering Dec. 18.

During Friday’s Game 1, the MLB and the MCU teamed up for a special preview of the upcoming movie, in which Pedro Pascal’s Mister Fantastic takes the mound for the ceremonial first pitch to Joseph Quinn’s Human Torch.

‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Teaser Unveiled: Chris Evans Is Coming Back As Steve Rogers

The preview also featured some familiar faces, including Chris Evans’ Steve Rogers, which causes Paul Rudd’s Ant-Man confusion over who to refer to as Captain America, with Anthony Mackie’s Sam Wilson now carrying the shield.

With the Tampa Bay Rays taking on the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 1 of the World Series on Friday, the MLB teased “an exclusive preview of Avengers: Doomsday ” would air during the game, which was broadcasted on Fox and streamed on Fox One.

Watch on Deadline

“Something’s coming …” the league’s post teased with a clip of the Avengers logo appearing in the green-tinted sky above Milwaukee’s American Family Field.

Worlds collide ⚾ An exclusive preview of Marvel's new Avengers movie assembles Bryce Harper, Freddie Freeman, Jacob Misiorowski, Junior Caminero and Randy Arozarena 👀 Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters everywhere December 18 pic.twitter.com/WX1YtKjAKt — MLB (@MLB) October 24, 2026

Premiering Dec. 18 in theaters, Avengers: Doomsday sees the multiverse collapse, forcing heroes from multiple Earths to unite against Doctor Doom (Robert Downey Jr).

The cast also includes Chris Hemsworth as Thor, Anthony Mackie as Captain America, Chris Evans as Steve Rogers, Paul Rudd as Ant-Man, Tenoch Huerta as Namor, Simu Liu as Shang-Chi, Letitia Wright as Black Panther, Kelsey Grammer as Beast, Danny Ramirez as Falcon, Winston Duke as M’Baku, Tom Hiddleton as Loki, Patrick Stewart as Professor X, Ian McKellen as Magneto, Alan Cumming as Nightcrawler, Rebecca Romijn as Mystique, James Marsden Cyclops, Channing Tatum Gambit and more.

When will The Housemaid’s Secret movie come out?

Watch on Deadline

The film has set its sight s on Dec. 17, 2027 to bow in theaters, exactly two years after the first film arrived in 2025. Production is set to take place this fall, as Paul Feig told Deadline at the Oscars .

Has production on The Housemaid’s Secret started yet?

Yes, the film is now in production, according to the movie’s Instagram account, which posted a video of the cast on set getting into costume and some reuniting.

View this post on Instagram

Who will be in the cast of The Housemaid’s Secret movie? Who is coming back from the first film?

Sydney Sweeney will reprise her role of Millie Calloway, who nannied and kept house for Nina Winchester (Amanda Seyfried) in the first film. Neither Seyfried’s Winchester nor Brandon Sklenar’s Andrew Winchester will be in the second film, with the latter meeting a fatal end in The Housemaid (2025). Michele Morrone will reprise his role of Enzo, the gardener.

As for new faces, Kirsten Dunst will star opposite Sweeney this second time around as Wendy Garrick. Paul Anthony Kelly ( Love Story ) will make his film debut as Wendy’s billionaire husband, Douglas Garrick. Brittany Snow has also joined the film as Marybeth.

Stephen Kalyn of Off Campus fame has been cast as Brock .

What is The Housemaid’s Secret about?

Sweeney’s Millie Calloway will take on a new housekeeping job for a woman she’s never allowed to see. Another locked door threatens to explore secrets much darker than Millie’s. The film will be based on Frieda McFadden’s sequel novel of the same name, which published in 2023.

Who else is behind The Housemaid’s Secret ?

Sweeney will also executive produce. Paul Feig is returning to direct from a script by Rebecca Sonnenshine, who adapted The Housemaid .

Producers will include Todd Lieberman of Hidden Pictures, Feig and Laura Fischer of Feig’s Pretty Dangerous Pictures, and Hidden Pictures’ Carly Elter and Alex Young. Author McFadden will also serve as an executive producer.

The film will be overseen by Lionsgate’s Chelsea Kujawa, who also oversaw the first film and brought the project into the studio, alongside Maria Ascanio. Robert Melnik negotiated deals for the studio.

University of Connecticut Offers a Funded MFA in Studio Art

Develop your creative practice. Gain teaching experience. Join a community of artists and educators.

The University of Connecticut's (UConn) MFA in Studio Art is a funded, two-year graduate program combining advanced studio research with substantial undergraduate teaching experience. Students pursue independent creative projects while gaining professional development as educators through graduate teaching assistantships.

Located within a major research university, the program supports a broad range of practices, including painting, drawing, printmaking, bookmaking, sculpture, installation, and performance. Students benefit from recently renovated studios, extensive facilities, close faculty mentorship, visiting artists, and a collaborative graduate community.

Situated in Southern New England, UConn offers convenient access to the major cultural centers of New York City and Boston, as well as the arts communities of Hartford, New Haven, and Providence.

Funding includes tuition remission, a stipend, and subsidized health insurance. The program culminates in an MFA thesis exhibition at UConn's William Benton Museum of Art.

Apply by January 15, 2027.

For more information, visit art.uconn.edu
